Cursed Blight

Designed and built solo, in a month

  • RoleGame Designer · Sole Developer
  • Team4, including me
  • TimelineAbout one month, start to release
  • StatusReleased
  • Built withUnity · C#
Play in browser on itch.io

The project

A short single-player old-school dungeon crawl steeped in unforgiving darkness. This was my first credited role as Game Designer, and I was also the only developer on it — I designed the gameplay, progression, narrative, art direction, menus, level, audio, the thumbnail and the trailer, and then wrote the game.

What I owned

  • Gameplay, progression and narrative design
  • Art direction, menus and level layout
  • Audio
  • Sole programmer — the entire build
  • Store thumbnail and trailer

A problem I solved

The whole game had to exist in roughly a month, and I had one or two days to produce the GDD before development started. That constraint *was* the design problem: anything I specified, I also had to build, so I could not afford to design a single system I was not confident would be both buildable in the time and actually fun.

So I designed to the constraint deliberately rather than designing something ambitious and cutting it later. I chose a form — old-school dungeon crawling — whose appeal comes from atmosphere, pacing and darkness rather than from deep systems that need weeks of tuning to feel good. Every mechanic I wrote down was one I already knew how to make work.

Result

Shipped on time and playable in the browser. Designing to the constraint instead of against it is the reason it is a finished game rather than an interesting fragment.

What I'd do differently

As a developer: structure the codebase so fewer systems depend on each other, write a proper pathfinding system, and make real use of culling. As a designer: make it shorter and pack more into it — a denser game would have reached further than a longer one.
